title: Navalny solidarity demonstration outside the Russian consulate, Gothenburg
reason: Reported attendance was about 20, below the 50-person inclusion threshold; the reported solidarity demand concerned Navalny and protesters in Russia, not Sweden's government.
notes: The contemporary Göteborgs-Posten body was read. It reports police dissolution under pandemic law, but the gathering remains out of scope on size and target.

title: Navalny solidarity demonstration outside the Russian Embassy, Stockholm
reason: The opened SVT report documents solidarity with Navalny and a demand for Putin to resign at the Russian Embassy; the reported target is the Russian state, not Sweden’s government. No attendance threshold is asserted for this exclusion.
notes: The opened SVT body confirms a calm 23 January gathering at the Russian Embassy and states solidarity with Navalny; a speaker called for Putin to resign and rights to be respected. Those stated demands target Russia, not Sweden. The source page’s number is not established here; the blocked Sveriges Radio item remains unread and no count/body claim is attributed to it. The Svenska Dagbladet page is search-only. Keep this as an exclusion lead with primary-source confirmation from SVT and an unresolved unread original SR source.

title: Threatened private-care strike notice, later cancelled
reason: A conditional workplace conflict with private employers, not a qualifying public gathering or demand to Sweden’s government. The employer association reports that the threatened actions were cancelled before their planned dates.
notes: Kommunal’s 5 January notice covered about 55,000 employees (not assembled people) and planned a first step from 15 January and strikes at selected workplaces from 22 January if no deal was reached. Almega reports that both parties accepted a mediator proposal on 14 January, cancelling both steps. The 15 January WSWS roundup says measures were planned; publication-time ordering relative to the agreement is unresolved. No actual action or public gathering is verified.

title: Threatened Pågatåg wildcat strike scheduled for 4 January; cancelled
reason: SVT reports the threatened work stoppage was cancelled before it began; the underlying dispute concerned a private employer, not a public gathering or demand to Sweden’s government.
notes: The private employer conflict was already reported on 30 December; SVT attributes a New Year’s Eve employee planning meeting to Sydsvenskan, without establishing a public gathering. On 2 January, SVT described a conditional strike threat for 4 January and said Seko advised workers not to participate. Sveriges Radio at 06:22 on 4 January still described a possible strike before an 11:00 meeting; later SVT reported the threat was called off after Arriva retained the safety representative. The approximately 100 coworkers outside the office are a separate gathering (X006); workforce counts and willingness are not strike turnout.

title: Online tenant-organizing meeting against market-rent reform
reason: This was an online meeting, not a physical public gathering. The reported participants cannot be counted as physical protest turnout; the article describes only planned demonstrations for April.
notes: Proletären reports more than 150 participants online and more than 170 registrations. Organizers discussed opposition to the government’s market-rent reform and planned future small demonstrations. No physical gathering in January is documented.

title: Coworkers gather outside Arriva office to support union safety representative
reason: The reported gathering supported a worker in a dispute with private employer Arriva; the source documents no demand to Sweden’s government or its policy.
notes: Contemporaneous SVT reports about 100 coworkers waiting outside Arriva’s office in Skåne before a meeting over Seko safety representative Ola Brunnström, and says he kept his job. The body does not name the office city or organizer and gives no precise end time. The 2022 Arbetet URL returned 403; its search excerpt is not used for occurrence or count.
